rationale: The badge shows '−50%', which the adjacent text 'on all seeds this week' does not give, yet alt is empty so the discount is lost.
A single grey horizontal line used as a divider; hiding it loses nothing.
The alt is a file name, 'IMG_2041.jpg', which conveys nothing about the image's content.
The alt describes a canvas garden bag, matching the image (labelled 'bag') and its 'Garden bag' product heading.

The alt 'Plan of the garden' names the image-map picture, and its regions are conveyed by the map's area links that a screen reader reaches with it; the placeholder name on the shed area is a separate area-level issue.
The icon is a shopping cart inside a link to cart.html, and the alt 'Cart' accurately names it and the link's purpose.
The area covers the region labelled 'Greenhouse' in the SVG and links to #greenhouse; its alt 'Greenhouse' matches the region and destination.
The area covers the 'Tool shed' region and links to #shed, but its alt is the placeholder 'Area 2', which does not say where the link leads.
The canvas draws content, but its aria-label is the generic word 'canvas' and its fallback is only a browser-support note, so nothing conveys what it shows.
The figcaption 'How to prune roses (2 minutes)' identifies the video, and the poster only shows a placeholder word with no further information to convey.
The embed's title is the file name 'garden-plan.svg', which does not describe the garden plan with its greenhouse and tool shed.
The button's name comes from aria-label 'button', a generic placeholder that does not say it checks delivery.
The alt 'Check delivery' states the button's action, which matches the form's purpose and the visible 'Check' text.
The alt is the file name 'btn_submit_02.png', which does not say the button checks delivery.
The fallback text 'Bar chart of seeds sold each month, highest in March' accurately describes the SVG bar chart for Jan to Mar, where March is tallest.
The link's name 'Search products' fits the magnifier icon and the link leads to the products page, so it describes the control's purpose rather than the picture.
The button's name 'Layer 1' is a drawing-tool leftover that says nothing about its share action.
'Demo Shop' is the site name in the header before the navigation, not a title for following body text.
'Delivery' titles the following paragraph about delivery times but is a bold paragraph, not a heading.
The title 'Page' is generic and does not say the page is about garden tools.
'Learn more' sits alone in its paragraph with no surrounding text saying it leads to the products page.
No visible text sits next to the postcode field and the next element is another input, not a button, so what to enter is given only by the hover-only title.
The field has only a placeholder 'Name', with no visible label or adjacent text, so once filled in nothing says what it is for.
The icon's alt 'Cart' repeats the link text 'Cart' beside it, so the link is read as 'Cart Cart' and the image could be alt="" with nothing lost.
The bold "Demo Shop" line is the site name in the header, followed by the navigation links rather than section content, so it is a name, not a section title.
The title "Returns and contact - Demo Shop" matches the main heading and the page content, which covers returns, downloads and a call-back form.
"Heading 2" is template placeholder text. The section after it is about returns, and the heading does not describe that.
Two tel fields are both labelled "Phone" under "Call us back", and nothing visible says how they differ or which one to fill in.
Two tel fields are both labelled "Phone" under "Call us back", and nothing visible says how they differ or which one to fill in.
The "Download" links lead to different files, a price list and a garden catalogue. The link text alone does not tell them apart, and the page has no setting to expand the names.
The "Download" links lead to different files, a garden catalogue and a price list. The link text alone does not tell them apart, and the page has no setting to expand the names.
"Read more" on its own does not say where the link leads, its name has no extra text, and the evidence shows no control that expands it.
"E-mail" and "Email address" differ only in hyphenation, so saying the visible label matches the start of the accessible name.
Both frames are titled "Shop page" but embed different pages (the home page and the products page), so their shared name does not tell them apart.
Both frames are titled "Shop page" but embed different pages (the products page and the home page), so their shared name does not tell them apart.
The button is an empty, colored 28px square with no visible text or icon, so its purpose is given only by the title tooltip.
The header navigation (Home, Products, Cart) and the footer navigation (About us, Jobs, Privacy) hold different links, and both are unnamed.
The footer navigation (About us, Jobs, Privacy) and the header navigation (Home, Products, Cart) hold different links, and both are unnamed.
The badge shows '−50%', which the nearby text ('on pots') does not give, so it is not decorative; alt="" marks it decorative and the aria-label 'Sale' does not convey the half-price information.
The single spanning first-row cell 'Opening hours' titles the whole table rather than heading a column or holding data, and the table has no caption and an empty accessible name.
The labels 'Standard' and 'Express' do not say what is chosen; the question 'How fast should it come?' is only a nearby paragraph with no fieldset/legend or named group.
The title 'Delivery and care - Demo Shop' matches the h1 'Delivery and care' and the page sections about ordering delivery and care guides.
The joined name 'Card number Name on card' runs two unrelated labels together; 'Name on card' belongs to a different field, so the name is misleading.
The 'Shop' and 'Search' links share accesskey 's' but go to different pages (index.html vs products.html), so one cannot be reached reliably by the shortcut.
The 'Search' and 'Shop' links share accesskey 's' but lead to different targets, so the shortcut may reach only one of them.
The empty th is the top-left corner cell above the row headers (Pots, Soil) and beside the column headers (Small, Large), so it heads no data cells.
The div has an onclick that navigates to products.html, so it acts as a link but is announced as an article with no name.
The h4 'Roses' comes straight after the h2 'Care guides' with no h3 between them, so the outline has a gap. It is a plain subsection, not a sidebar or a card set at a fixed level.
The block at the top holds the site name 'Demo Shop' and main links, so it is the page header, yet the only landmark is main and there is no banner.
alt="" says decorative but aria-label 'Sale' exposes it as an image; whichever was intended, the markup conflicts and the exposed name does not match the '−50%' content.
The site header with the site name and Shop/Search links is real page content and lies outside every landmark (only main exists).
The title "Reviews - Demo Shop" matches the main heading "Reviews" and names the site, so it says what the page is about.
In portrait, main (all the page content) is set to display:none and only a "Please turn your device to landscape" message shows. A reviews page does not need one orientation, so this is F100.
The stars carry the rating, and the only text beside them is "Rated", which gives no value. At 1.43:1 they fall below the 3:1 that information-bearing graphics need.
The arrow sits inside a link whose visible text "Next page" already gives its meaning, so the arrow only decorates.
The alt 'Canvas garden bag' matches the heading and what the image shows (a bag), so it identifies the image accurately in context.
The image is the only content of a link to ../index.html, but its alt describes the picture ('Plan of the shop's garden') rather than the link's destination or purpose.
'Demo Shop' is the site name in the header, followed by the navigation, not a title for a section of text.
The plan shows the Greenhouse and Tool shed, and ordinary text links to index.html#greenhouse and #shed sit right below; the link itself also works with Enter to index.html.

The .terms box is 60px high and 320px wide with overflow:auto, and its six sentences need several more lines than fit, so content is hidden; it has no tabindex, so it is not keyboard-scrollable in all browsers.
The hover handlers only toggle the link's text decoration, a cosmetic effect; the link itself works with the keyboard.
Hovering the image writes product information ('Holds 20 litres, washable at 30 degrees.') into the page, and the image cannot take keyboard focus, so keyboard users cannot get that information.
The onfocus handler calls this.blur() unconditionally, so focus is removed as soon as the tabbable Cart link receives it.
The title 'Garden bag - Demo Shop' matches the page's h1 'Garden bag' and names the site.
The Back to top link is positioned off-screen by the 'offscreen' class and the checker found no focus rule bringing it into view, so focus lands on an invisible element.
A focusable button is nested inside a link, both with the name 'Buy'; the inner control is not reliably reachable or announced on its own and its activation is ambiguous.
The checkbox is checked but has aria-checked='false', so assistive technology reports unchecked; nothing in the evidence shows a script correcting it.
The #returns content is fully shown with no hidden attribute while the toggle says aria-expanded='false', so screen reader users are told it is collapsed.
The only content outside landmarks is the 'Skip to content' link, which needs no landmark.
No element with id 'content' exists (targetExists false; main has no id), so the skip link does not move focus past the header and navigation.
tabindex='1' on a footer Privacy link makes it the first Tab stop, ahead of the skip link and 10 other stops, pulling focus out of reading order.
'Demo Shop' is the site name in the header followed by navigation, not a section title for text.
'Offers - Demo Shop' matches the page's main heading 'Offers' and states its purpose.
Three mouse-operable controls (Account menu, Fern tile, Cactus tile) cannot take focus; also nav links show no focus indicator and order is illogical.
The Account menu span has a click handler but cannot take focus, and no stop in the focus walk offers the same account action.
#tile-cactus has role button but is listed as unreachable (cannot take focus) and is never a Tab stop; no other stop offers the same function.
Focus starts on 'Seeds and bulbs' near the bottom of main (y 850), then jumps back to the header navigation and then to links higher up in main, so the order does not follow the reading order.
The focus walk shows the Home link changes nothing on focus (changesOnFocus empty, 0 pixels changed), so focus is not visible.
The focus walk shows the Products link changes nothing on focus (changesOnFocus empty, 0 pixels changed), so focus is not visible.
The focus walk shows the Cart link changes nothing on focus (changesOnFocus empty, 0 pixels changed), so focus is not visible.
On focus the Help link changes background, text colour and underline (682 pixels changed), so focus remains visible without an outline.
Stops 2-4 (Home, Products, Cart) show no visible change on focus, and stops 6-7 are entirely covered by the sticky header, so focus is not always visible.
Stops 6 and 7 ('Roses, 20% off', 'Tulips, 3 for 2') take focus with coveredShare 1 under header#top-bar, i.e. entirely hidden.
Stops 6 and 7 are covered by header#top-bar with coveredShare 1 while focused, so they are hidden (entirely, hence also partly).
The Home link shows no focus indicator: 0 pixels changed at 3:1 against 244 needed, meets false.
The Products link shows no focus indicator: 0 pixels changed at 3:1 against 336 needed, meets false.
The Cart link shows no focus indicator: 0 pixels changed at 3:1 against 192 needed, meets false.
The Help link's focus change covers 584 pixels at 3:1 or more, above the 204 needed, and meets is true.
Nothing changes on the Home link on focus, so there is no indicator to meet 3:1.

Nothing changes on the Cart link on focus, so there is no indicator to meet 3:1.
The Help link's focus change has 584 of 682 changed pixels at 3:1 or more, far more than a one-pixel outline (106), so it is clearly visible.
'Demo Shop' sits in the header just before the main navigation and reads as the site name, not a title for following section text.
'Garden gloves - Demo Shop' matches the main heading 'Garden gloves'.
The Size guide dialog cannot be closed with the keyboard: its close control is a non-focusable span and Escape does not close it.
The Size guide dialog does not take focus (focus stays on the link) and focus then leaves it after a few Tabs, so a modal does not keep focus.
Every Tab stop shows an outline change on focus and none is hidden or covered.

The pixel measurement says nearly the whole box (nearTextShare 1) is drawn almost in the text colour. That means the near-white gradient is about the same colour as the white banner text, so contrast is far below 4.5:1.
White 18px regular text on the dark green gradient has a median ratio of 14.08 and a 10th percentile of 11.39. Only 4% of pixels fall below 4.5:1, which fits antialiased edges.
The title 'Seeds - Demo Shop' matches the page's only heading, 'Seeds', and names the site, so it says what the page is about.
The teaser has a fixed height of 2.6em with overflow hidden. With the spacing applied it shows only 1 of its 2 lines, and the context has no 'read more' link or other way to reach the full text.

The !important letter-spacing comes from a style sheet rule, not an inline style, so a user style sheet or an inline !important style can still override it. 'SALE' is one short word that reads fine either way.

A later viewport tag (width=device-width, initial-scale=1) replaces the restricting one, and current browsers apply the last viewport tag, so pinch zoom is not blocked. Browsers have not always agreed on this, so confidence is moderate.
